parsedVerdict.reasoning: The rule holds. All three files are immutable domain value objects for the order model, so the module covers one concern. OrderLine builds its quantity through Quantity.of, so the quantity bounds are defined only in Quantity.ts. OrderStatus.ts holds the status list, the allowed transitions (canTransition) and the stock effect of each status (stockEffectOf). Each of those rules is defined once. OrderStatus is a string union with pure functions instead of a class. That suits an enumeration and does not get around any abstraction in the module. One small difference: Quantity throws InvalidValueError itself, while OrderLine uses the shared guards. Quantity's range check is specific to Quantity and does not repeat any guard, so this is not duplication.
